span_text: in the event that Bellicum reasonably determines to reject a proposed Material Change (including a Miltenyi-Requested Change), Miltenyi will continue to supply the applicable Miltenyi Product without such change after expiry of the said 6-month period and during the Term of this Agreement, or until Bellicum has secured an alternate source of supply from a Third Party manufacturer
reason:
SUB-SENTENCE exclusion: the segment is KEPT and yields item C04-07 from the same sentence's proviso. This clause alone is excluded.

GROUND. 'Miltenyi will continue to supply the applicable Miltenyi Product without such change after expiry of THE SAID 6-MONTH PERIOD' -- a sectionless backward anaphor whose antecedent is in subsection (e) or (g), outside the segment (verified mechanically: '6-month' occurs exactly once in the segment, in the reference itself). It supplies the OPERATIVE START BOUND of a scored field, §5 clause 6.

PRECEDENT CALIBRATION, against all six existing cross-reference exclusions rather than argued in the abstract. EXCLUDING side, where the out-of-segment reference carries OPERATIVE CONTENT: C15-046 ('in the manner aforesaid' -- a backward reference with no section number, the duty's method unreadable), C11-079 (the gating consent mechanism outside), C04-018 and C04-118 (prices and thresholds outside). KEEPING side, where it qualifies SCOPE DETAIL ONLY: C03-01 item 4, 'as set forth in the terms of the Maintenance Addendum' -- reviewer-confirmed as the right distinction. This clause is C15-046's shape exactly. WHEN the duty starts is not scope detail in a clause whose whole content is 'will continue to supply ... after expiry of' it.

NOT A DIFFICULTY DODGE, stated because §2.1 step 4's sample exists to catch exactly that. This clause is also the hardest thing in the segment (see observation 1). The exclusion stands on the cross-reference ground ALONE, which is independent of that difficulty, and the segment and its clean item are kept rather than excluded whole -- the cheaper move, which would have lost an item with a direct locked precedent (C04-02).

observations.label: INSTANCE ONE (of two) -- multi-element temporal composition, no §8 tag exists
observations.status: RECORDED, NOT ACTED ON. Not the ground of this exclusion.
observations.note:
A GENUINE COMPOSITION GAP, DISTINCT FROM §8.11's, AND THIS IS THE FIRST RECORDED INSTANCE. The excluded clause's timing is THREE elements composed: 'after expiry of the said 6-month period' AND 'during the Term of this Agreement' OR 'until Bellicum has secured an alternate source of supply from a Third Party manufacturer'.

WHY IT IS NOT §8.11's lead_time_unrepresentable. §8.11's decisive test was that 'granting free composition of all five v1 forms does NOT rescue the clause', because no v1 form pairs a duration with a direction. HERE THE TEST COMES OUT THE OTHER WAY: each of the three elements HAS a v1 form on its own -- RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER(after, ...), DURING(...), and a terminal bound. Free composition WOULD rescue this clause. What IR v1 lacks is not a form for any element but THE ABILITY TO HOLD MORE THAN ONE TEMPORAL AT ALL: ast.Obligation carries a single temporal field. So the two gaps are different mechanisms and lead_time_unrepresentable must not be reused for this one.

IT FAILS SILENTLY, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS AND WAS VERIFIED BY EXECUTION AGAINST THE PRODUCTION CLASSIFIER, not read off the regex. ir_compile._RELATIVE_RE is '^(before|after)\s+(.+)$' -- greedy -- so the whole phrase returns AFTER "expiry of the said 6-month period and during the Term of this Agreement, or until Bellicum has secured an alternate source of supply from a Third Party manufacturer": it COMPILES, swallowing the other two bounds into the trigger string and misstating the duty's window. It does not raise UNMAPPABLE_TEMPORAL. Contrast the isolated bounds, which DO return None: 'during the Term of this Agreement' -> None, 'until Bellicum has secured an alternate source...' -> None.

CANDIDATE §10 AMENDMENT, DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED ON ONE INSTANCE (§22.1's own discipline -- a kind must not be ruled on a sample of one): a temporal_composition tag, kind REPRESENTATIONAL under §8.10's test (IR v1 has no form for the composed whole; this is not a surface pattern rejecting input the IR could hold), direction INCOMPLETENESS or a misstatement -- undecided, and the greedy-swallow behaviour above is why it is not obviously INCOMPLETENESS.

FOR THE FUTURE SESSION THAT FINDS THIS: cite it as INSTANCE ONE. A second independent instance is the forcing function for the amendment. Search key: temporal composition, greedy _RELATIVE_RE, C04-051.

INSTANCE TWO HAS ARRIVED (2026-09-20): C04-072, segments/C04-072.json, observation C04-072#temporal-composition. It fails through a DIFFERENT REGEX -- greedy _WITHIN_RE rather than greedy _RELATIVE_RE -- and the shared cause is the TRAILING '(.+)$' CAPTURE both patterns end with, so the silent-swallow is a property of the classifier's SHAPE and not a quirk of one pattern. A fix aimed at one regex would leave the other. The forcing function for the §10 amendment is therefore met; the reviewer has scoped it as its OWN ruling session (option (a)) rather than inside an annotation pass, with direction deliberately not pre-selected.

RULED 2026-09-23 -- F21, guideline v0.63, §8.12. The tag is `temporal_composition`, kind REPRESENTATIONAL, and DIRECTION IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASSIGNED (see below). TWO CLAIMS IN THE NOTE ABOVE DO NOT SURVIVE EXECUTION AND ARE CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. (1) 'each of the three elements HAS a v1 form on its own' is FALSE for this instance: run through the production classifier, 'after expiry of the said 6-month period' classifies, but 'during the Term of this Agreement' -> None and 'until Bellicum has secured an alternate source...' -> None -- which the note itself measures three paragraphs later without reconciling the two statements. ONE of three elements has a form, not three. The distinction from §8.11 SURVIVES the correction but rests on instance two, where two of three elements do classify. Mechanically, 'until <event>' has no v1 form at any layer -- DuringTemporal is {start: DateRef, end: DateRef}, so there is no end-only slot and no trigger-typed terminus -- so that element is itself §8.11-shaped, and this instance is a MIXED case rather than a pure composition gap. (2) The note's ground for leaving direction open -- 'the greedy-swallow yields a trigger string asserting a WRONG window' -- measures the PIPELINE'S output, where §8.10.1's test is whether GOLD departs from the document. Gold never swallows: it records one element and drops the rest. So 'misstatement' is not a candidate direction here at all. DIRECTION IS STILL DEFERRED, on a DIFFERENT and stronger ground: it varies by instance and even within one item. Dropping a NARROWING bound (this clause's 'during the Term' and 'until...') leaves the IR claiming the duty runs longer than the contract imposes -- OVERSTATING; dropping an ADDITIVE deadline (instance two's recurring annual forecast) leaves it claiming less -- INCOMPLETENESS. C04-08 does both. F21 asks the general question (per-tag or per-item direction) and the vocabulary records DIRECTION_DEFERRED explicitly, so the deferral cannot be read as an omission. THIS CLAUSE REMAINS EXCLUDED and yields no item, so the tag reaches it only as the precedent it set.

observations.label: First use of the EXCLUDED disposition at sub-sentence granularity
observations.note: §2.7 defines EXCLUDED (carrying exclusion_log_id) as one of its disposition values, and across all 22 committed segment files before batch 4 it had ZERO uses -- measured, not assumed: NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING 38, ANNOTATED 36, AMBIGUOUS 3, NOT_ANNOTATABLE 2, EXCLUDED 0. Sub-sentence DISPOSITION is already established practice (C14-076 disposes [420:506] NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING inside a sentence that also yields item C14-06); sub-sentence EXCLUSION was not. segment_text: (h) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (e) and (g), in the event that Bellicum reasonably determines to reject a proposed Material Change (including a Miltenyi-Requested Change), Miltenyi will continue to supply the applicable Miltenyi Product without such change after expiry of the said 6-month period and during the Term of this Agreement, or until Bellicum has secured an alternate source of supply from a Third Party manufacturer; provided, however, that the Parties will discuss in good faith, reflecting the change in circumstances contemplated by this Section 3.2(h), and agree in writing upon commercially reasonable terms to be set forth in an amendment to this Agreement to reflect any demonstrable increased cost and effort (if any) resulting from the manufacture of unchanged Miltenyi Product solely for Bellicum, including (as an example) any applicable adjustments to Forecasts, Lead Times, production cycles, batch sizes, Delivery Dates, Product Prices, or other relevant issues. If the Parties cannot reach agreement regarding such amendment, any obligations of Bellicum in relation to a Forecast for the affected Miltentyi Product in months 7-12 of the applicable Monthly Forecast, and any limitations regarding forecast variances, as each of these are set forth in Article 5, will not apply to a Miltenyi Product produced after implementation of such Material Change (i.e., one that replaces such affected (unchanged) Miltenyi Product), and Miltenyi shall be relieved from any obligations to supply such affected (unchanged) Miltenyi Product under this Agreement after the period described in the first sentence of this subsection (h) ends. For clarity, in no event shall Miltenyi be required to manufacture, supply or sell an existing Miltenyi Product to which a Required Change must be applied.

rule: section 2, section 3.2 (no obligation-bearing clause -- Agreement-as-subject counterparts boilerplate)
reason:
Counterparts/execution boilerplate. Four clauses, ZERO obligation-bearing, so §2's 'contains 1-3 obligation-bearing clauses' eligibility test fails at zero. (1) 'This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts' and (4) the elliptical 'and may be executed through exchange of original signatures or electronic copies (PDF)' are AGREEMENT-AS-SUBJECT -- §8.8's own named excluded class and §3.2's future-fact rule; no party performs an act. (2) 'each of which need not contain the signature of more than one Party' has a non-party subject (the counterparts) and NEGATES A REQUIREMENT rather than commanding conduct -- §8.8.1's class, where 'need not X' is not MUST_NOT X. (3) 'all such counterparts taken together shall constitute one and the same agreement' is a copular status statement, subject a thing. The word 'Party' occurs once in the segment and only as the object of 'the signature of', never as an actor.

DIRECT PRECEDENT: batch 2's E01-040 -- 'Counterparts/execution boilerplate. Subject is the Agreement, not a party ... section 3.2's future-fact rule. Same shape as batch 1's E03-051 exclusion.' Same rule string, same class, same disposition. Also consistent with C22-045, C10-029, C17-038 and E08-046, the four other committed 'subject is a thing' boilerplate exclusions.
segment_text: 20.7 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which need not contain the signature of more than one Party but all such counterparts taken together shall constitute one and the same agreement, and may be executed through exchange of original signatures or electronic copies (PDF).

reason:
Two sentences, ZERO obligation-bearing, so §2's 'contains 1-3 obligation-bearing clauses' eligibility test fails at zero and §2's first exclusion row (definitions) applies.

S1 IS A DEFINITION. '"Commencement Date" shall be the first day of the Month following the date Transporter notifies Customer that (i) ... (ii) ... (iii) ...' -- the subject is a QUOTED DEFINED TERM, not a party, and 'shall be' is copular. Clauses (i)-(iii) are all status conditions ('is operational', 'are in effect'), not duties. The embedded 'the date Transporter notifies Customer' is a TEMPORAL ANCHOR FOR THE DEFINITION, not an obligation: nothing in the sentence says Transporter SHALL notify -- it fixes when the defined date falls IF and WHEN notification happens. Precedents: C14-003 ('"CONTROL" shall mean...'), C05-009, E03-003, C04-150.

S2 IS EXCLUDED ON POLARITY, BEFORE ITS COMPLEMENT IS REACHED. 'Transporter WILL NOT BE RESPONSIBLE FOR delays to the Commencement Date due to the action or inaction of Customer or Third Party Operators.' §8.8.4's PRIOR FILTER 1 (polarity, §8.8.1) removes a negated be/remain responsible/liable clause regardless of complement -- the worked case is C04-163, 'shall not be responsible for payments', excluded even though its complement is an act nominalisation that would otherwise read RENDER. The two axes are independent and neither answers for the other. Recorded for completeness: this clause's complement ('delays') would read ABSORB under §8.8.4's limb (b) risk allocation in any event, so both axes agree -- but polarity is the operative ground and is sufficient alone.
segment_text: "Commencement Date" shall be the first day of the Month following the date Transporter notifies Customer that (i) the Transportation System is operational to the extent necessary to commence commercial service with respect to the receipt of Customer Gas at the Point of Receipt at the tailgate of the Lincoln Parish Plant and delivery of such Gas to the Points of Delivery located downstream of the Lincoln Parish Plant, (ii) the Lincoln Parish Plant is operational to the extent necessary to commence commercial service with respect to the receipt and processing of Customer Gas, and (iii) the Points of Delivery listed on Exhibit A that are owned by Transporter or its Affiliate are operational and all necessary interconnect agreements with Interconnecting Pipelines necessary to deliver Gas to such Points of Delivery are in effect to the extent necessary to commence commercial service with respect to the delivery (but, for the avoidance of doubt, not the further downstream transportation) of Customer's Gas. Transporter will not be responsible for delays to the Commencement Date due to the action or inaction of Customer or Third Party Operators.

reason:
Severability boilerplate. ONE sentence, ZERO obligation-bearing clauses, so §2's 1-3 band fails at zero.

THE ONLY PARTY-SUBJECT PREDICATE IS 'the Parties AGREE THAT ...', AND WHAT IS AGREED IS A STATUS PROPOSITION, NOT CONDUCT. The that-clause reads 'the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall remain in full force' -- subject 'the remaining provisions', a thing; 'shall remain' copular. Nobody is commanded to do or refrain from anything. §3.8.1's not-branch-1 list names this class in terms -- 'an interpretive or savings provision with a non-party subject' -- and its own worked example is 'no such SEVERABILITY shall be effective'. Direct precedents: C10-029 (severability boilerplate, 'subject is that provision, a legal-effect/status statement, not a party's duty'), C02-062 (survival-of-obligations savings), C22-045 (entire-agreement), C17-038 (survival).

A CONSISTENCY CHECK ON THE 2026-09-20 E03-03 RULING, PERFORMED DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because that ruling could have been read as opening this class. 'The Parties agree' is itself a present-tense performative, and E03-03 ruled that a performative IS obligation-bearing where it survives §3.2.1's rationale. It does not survive here: the reviewer's ground for E03-03 was that 'guarantees' creates a STANDING CONTINGENT EXPOSURE to a future failure, which S3i's deeming provision exists to make checkable. 'Agree that' leaves nothing behind -- the agreeing completes at execution and no future state is monitorable, so §3.2.1 excludes it exactly as before. The E03-03 ruling DISCRIMINATES rather than swallowing the performative class, and this segment is the first instance confirming that.

The two 'if' clauses are conditions on a legal effect, not on a duty, and there is no duty for them to gate.
segment_text: 3.33 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is determined to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the Parties agree that the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall remain in full force if both the economic and legal substance of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement are not affected in any manner that is materially adverse to either Party by severing the provision determined to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable.

rule: section 2, section 3.8.1 (interpretive/savings provision; no obligation-bearing clause)
reason:
Severability boilerplate. ZERO obligation-bearing clauses, so §2's 1-3 band fails at zero. Same class as this batch's C03-102 exclusion and batch 3's C10-029.

Three predicates, every one with a THING as its subject: (1) 'such provision shall be severed', (2) 'and shall be inoperative', (3) 'and the remainder of this Agreement shall remain operative and binding on the Parties'. All are legal-effect / status statements about contract provisions. C10-029 is the direct precedent -- 'that provision or part-provision shall ... be deemed not to form part of this agreement -- subject is that provision (a contract clause), a legal-effect/status statement, not a party's duty'. §3.8.1's not-branch-1 list names the class and uses a severability clause as its own worked example.

§3.5.3 WAS CONSIDERED AND DOES NOT RESCUE IT, recorded because that is the rule that could have. 'shall be severed' is an agentless passive, and §3.5.3 exists to admit agentless obligations with obligor ABSENT. But §3.5.3 governs agentless PERFORMANCE passives -- a duty someone must render with no by-agent stated. Severance is a legal effect that operates by force of the clause itself; no party performs it, and the notional subject is a contract provision rather than a thing acted on by a party. 'The Parties' appears once, as the object of 'binding on', never as an actor.

The 'If any provision ... is held illegal or unenforceable in a judicial proceeding' clause conditions a legal effect, not a duty, and there is no duty for it to gate.
segment_text: 14. Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held illegal or unenforceable in a judicial proceeding, such provision shall be severed and shall be inoperative, and the remainder of this Agreement shall remain operative and binding on the Parties.
